newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Matsushita to focus on emerging markets.
newsitem.headline: Matsushita to focus on emerging markets.

text.p: Matsushita Electric Industrial Co will increase investments in Asia's emerging markets while it consolidates existing operations in Southeast Asia, executive vice president Masayuki Matsushita said on Tuesday.

"We are not thinking of establishing more companies in Southeast Asia as we are in Vietnam and India," Matsushita told reporters, adding the company had sufficient operations in Southeast Asia and would focus investments in new markets.
"The plan for Southeast Asia is mainly to have each company become more profitable," Matsushita added.
He declined to disclose the amount of capital Matsushita Electric would invest in Vietnam except that plans were underway for the setting up of more offices within the next three years.
Matsushita was here for the International Advisory Council (IAC) meeting organised by the Economic Development Board.
He said the company aimed to only widen product development in existing markets such as Southeast Asia, and also China.
He said factories in China were newly established and the near-term objective was to establish "self-sufficiency," but adding more operations by the year 2000 were not ruled out.
The consumer electronics giant has 31 manufacturing plants, two sales offices and a supporting company in China.
Matsushita Electric's production in Asia accounts for about 60 percent of total overseas production, and Singapore output makes up about half around 30 percent, Matsushita said.
Matsushita Electric sells its products under the National, Panasonic and Technics brand names.
On Tuesday in Japan, Matsushita Electric released results for the October-December period showing group net profit jumped 35 percent from a year ago to 45.3 billion yen.
Operating profit surged 52 percent to 119.7 billion yen.
Matsushita said the company will diversify to stay on top of the competition, especially against old rival Sony.
"We do not think our company is only a consumer electronics company...we have many competitors, in communications, computers and components industries," Matsushita said.
